newsitem.title: USA: Most US Gulf refiners eschew pricey foreign crudes.
newsitem.headline: Most US Gulf refiners eschew pricey foreign crudes.

text.p: Most refiners on the U.S. Gulf Coast eschewed pricey transatlantic crudes on Monday, preferring to shop around closer to home, traders said.

The July spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent narrowed to around $1.10 a barrel on Monday. The WTI/dated Brent spread was at a relatively broad $1.70 a barrel, after a dated cargo for June 17-19 sold for July Brent minus 62 cents a barrel.
Whatever the spreads, refiners were seen shunning North Sea and West African barrels.
"Basically the arbitrage is pretty well shut. And the refiners here don't really need the crude so there's no point in forcing it open," said one crude seller.
Brent was heard offered around 40-45 cents under WTI/Cushing, down from a 70-cent discount late last week, traders said.

A U.S. equity producer was offering a cargo each of Qua Iboe and Brass River for end-June arrival, asking around dated Brent plus $1.80 a barrel and dated Brent plus $2.00, respectively, traders said.
Latn American offerings seemed to be turning more heads, despite high Caribbean freight rates.

Last Friday, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol sold a Cusiana cargo for July 15-19 loading to a U.S. company for $1.39 a barrel under August WTI/Cushing, steady with a previous Cusiana deal last Wednesday, traders said.
A European company also sold a Vasconia cargo for first-decade July delivery for $3.47 a barrel under WTI/Cushing.
"Everything versus North Sea and West Africa looks cheaper right now," a Gulf Coast buyer said.
